proof: Let n=2^k, theta=pi/(4n), zeta=exp(2i theta). zeta has irreducible polynomial X^(2n)+1 (its shift by 1 is 2-Eisenstein), hence degree 2n. i=zeta^n; t=-i(zeta-1)/(zeta+1) is real, and zeta=(1+it)/(1-it). Q(zeta)=Q(t,i), [Q(t,i):Q(t)]=2, so [Q(t):Q]=n. The displayed degree-n polynomial vanishes by tan(n theta)=1 and is therefore minimal.
finiteness_proof: The selected slopes obey y0=1, s_i=sqrt(1+y_(i-1)^2)>0, y_i=y_(i-1)/(1+s_i)=tan(pi/2^(i+2)). For the relaxed equations both square-root signs give 2^k distinct real slopes; the inverse y_(i-1)=2*y_i/(1-y_i^2) recovers all preceding coordinates. No conjugate equals 0, +/-1 or +/-i, so all line/angle nonzero factors and denominators stay nonzero. The genuine interior bisectors define one configuration.
